newsitem.title: UK: Northern Irish police launch murder probe.
newsitem.headline: Northern Irish police launch murder probe.

text.p: Police in Northern Ireland launched a murder hunt on Tuesday after a man's body, with head wounds, was found beside a burned-out car near Randalstown in County Antrim, security sources said.
They said they did not know if the killing was linked to the British province's long-running guerrilla conflict. An autopsy would be held to determine whether he had been shot.
In a separate development in the Irish Republic, police were planning to question an injured republican suspect after a botched guerrilla bomb attack in Northern Ireland.
Irish security sources said officers were at a northwestern hospital where the man was likely to be arrested for questioning when discharged after treatment.
Last Friday guerrillas en route to a target dumped a bomb in the centre of Belfast after the detonator exploded prematurely, according to police sources there.
No one admitted responsibilty but it was thought to have been done by extremists in one of several groups fighting to end British rule.
RTE, Ireland's national news network, reported that the man had severe burns on his arms, face and hands.

It quoted Irish security sources as saying that the man, in his 40s and from nationalist West Belfast, had had links with the outlawed Irish Republican Army but was thought to have switched support to a splinter group, the Irish Continuity Army Council, which has carried out several bombings.
